topic.title: Juicero's Juicer Only Pressed Its Own Packs

title: Juicero's $699 Juicer Only Squeezed Its Own Packs
description:
Why did a juicer from Silicon Valley cost $699?
Juicero's press, its juice packs at $5 to $7 each, and the day reporters tried their own hands, told from the reporting.
Sources: Fortune, CBS News (Sep 2017).
Based on public records and reporting. Not financial or legal advice.

cta: The machine or the packs: which one sank Juicero? Comment

lines.text: Juicero sold a $699 juicer that only pressed its own packs.
Each pack held chopped fruit and vegetables, sold for $5 to $7, one glass at a time. So why buy the machine?
It launched in San Francisco, backed by Google's venture arm and Kleiner Perkins.
In January, Juicero cut the press from $699 to $399.
Then in April, Bloomberg reporters skipped the press and squeezed the packs with their bare hands.
Their hands got nearly as much juice out, and faster. So who still needed the machine?
That September, Juicero shut down for good.
By then, investors had put about $120M into a juicer that two bare hands could match.
The machine or the packs: which one sank Juicero? Next time you squeeze a lemon, remember,

Re-review after rewrite: the order is now right. The January 2017 cut from $699 to $399 comes before Bloomberg's April 2017 hand test and the shutdown on 1 Sep 2017 (CBS News: cut in January; Fortune: shutdown on 1 Sep 2017). The bridge 'who still needed the machine?' no longer suggests the cut was a response to the test. $699, $399 and $5-7 confirmed on the Fortune page; about $120M from Google Ventures and Kleiner Perkins confirmed on CBS News (verify item met). 'Nearly as much, and faster' matches Bloomberg's 2017-04-19 test as reported by Snopes, Core77 and Fortune. fact2 as_of 2017-07-31 is accepted: $399 was the price on that date and it is not shown on screen. The shutdown beat's Fortune headline matches the article and the empty-office photo is generic. Disclaimer present in the description. Style note: 'six hundred ninety nine dollars juicer' sounds awkward when spoken.

Beats result->cut: 'So what could Juicero do now? Juicero dropped the press from $699 to $399' presents the price cut as a response to Bloomberg's April 2017 hand-squeeze test, but the cut came in January 2017, three months BEFORE the test (CBS News 2017-09-01: lowered 'from $700 to $400 in January'; Fortune 2017-09-01 links the cut to a Jan 17 2017 story). Reorder: put the cut before the April test (e.g. 'In January it cut the price to $399. Then in April, Bloomberg reporters...') and drop the 'what could Juicero do now' bridge, or say only 'That September, it shut down' after the test. Also set fact2 as_of to 2017-01 (currently 2017-07-31).

Confirmed otherwise: $699 launch price and $399 after the cut and $5-7 packs on fortune.com/2017/09/01/juicero-is-shutting-down (shutdown 1 Sep 2017, Bloomberg April 2017); about $120M from Google Ventures and Kleiner Perkins on cbsnews.com/philadelphia/news/400-juicer-shuts-down (verify item satisfied: 'about'); 'nearly as much, and faster' matches Bloomberg 2017-04-19 as reported by Snopes/Core77/Fortune (7.5 oz by hand in ~90s vs 8 oz in ~2 min by machine). Disclaimer present at end of description. Style note: 'six hundred ninety nine dollars juicer' reads awkwardly when spoken.
